ORIE 5260 / PART 2 — COURSE PPT ADJUSTED BASELINE

The course PPT approach: adjusted baseline

sᵢ,ₜ = sign(Σₖ₌₀¹¹ rᵢ,ₜ₋ₖ)
σ̂ᵢ,ₜ = Std(rᵢ,₁:ₜ) × √12
wᵢ,ₜ = (1 / Nₜ) × sᵢ,ₜ × 0.40 / σ̂ᵢ,ₜ
  • Expanding volatility requires at least 36 valid monthly observations.
  • Weights formed in month t earn returns in t+1; rebalance monthly.
  • Static uses the same volatility and eligibility, always long.

strategy_backtest_adj.py follows the course PPT approach. The 40% parameter scales individual markets; it is not a portfolio volatility target.

Execution timing and assumptions

Formation month tExecution month t+1
Signal and risk estimates use data through texecution_weights = weights.shift(1)
Construct equally allocated inverse-volatility positionsRₚ,ₜ₊₁ = Σ wᵢ,ₜ rᵢ,ₜ₊₁

  • Missing realized returns for held positions are filled with zero.

ORIE 5260 / PART 3 — ROLLING BASELINE

Compounded versus summed momentum signals

Both baselines compound wealth; their historical signal aggregation differs

Example: +20%, then −18%CalculationPosition direction
Rolling compound signal1.20 × 0.82 − 1 = −1.6%Short
Adjusted sum signal20% − 18% = +2.0%Long
  • Large swings can cause opposite signal directions.
  • Risk-window and eligibility differences also affect portfolio results.
  • A controlled signal-only test would hold all other choices fixed.

Why do the static correlations differ?

ComparisonPPT / adjustedRolling
Corr with own static0.0800.385
Signal / volatilitySum / expandingCompound / trailing 12m
Sample1976–20141970.02–2014
  • Possible mechanism: shared recent-volatility scaling may increase co-movement between rolling TSMOM and static.
  • Signal signs, eligibility, and sample periods also differ; their effects are not isolated.
  • Each static benchmark is different. Lower correlation alone does not imply a better strategy.

Observed gap, untested explanation. Align samples and eligibility, then change one component at a time.

ORIE 5260 / PART 5 — ENHANCEMENTS AND CONCLUSIONS

Four completed PPT / adjusted experiments

ExperimentChange from baselinePurpose
E1: EWMA volatility6-month half-life; keep 36-month eligibilityRespond faster to changing risk
E2: Asset-class budgetEqual allocation across valid classes; 1/N within classReduce market-count imbalance
E3: Multiple lookbacksAverage 1-, 3-, 6-, and 12-month signsReduce dependence on one horizon
E4: CombinedE1 + E2 + E3Test whether improvements combine

These experiments have results. Full covariance models, portfolio volatility targeting, and walk-forward evaluation remain next-stage work.

ORIE 5260 / PART 5 — ENHANCEMENTS AND CONCLUSIONS

Findings: credible signal, incomplete risk model

  • Predictiveness: the 12-month signal has a 54.4% hit rate and supportive HAC evidence.
  • Historical performance: PPT / adjusted CAGR of 10.64% and Sharpe of 0.97.
  • Return sources: all classes and both directions contribute; commodities and longs dominate.
  • Risk gap: predicted volatility of 6.82% versus subsequent realized volatility of 9.78%.
  • Implementation: leverage, turnover, zero-filled returns, and omitted costs matter.
  • Experiments: EWMA improves results; multiple horizons reduce drawdowns; effects are not additive.
midterm_report.md；module outputs29 / 30
ORIE 5260 / PART 5 — ENHANCEMENTS AND CONCLUSIONS

Next steps and reproducibility

  • Add covariance forecasts and validate future fixed-weight risk.
  • Test portfolio volatility targeting, leverage caps, and volatility floors.
  • Align baseline samples; use walk-forward tests and realistic costs.
  • Resolve RL and outlier sensitivity; expand futures-relevant factors.

Reproduce rolling and adjusted baselines separately. Detailed attribution and risk validation use standardized adjusted-baseline outputs.
